blocks.title: PDFCraft in the activity panel
blocks.description: Read, reorder, merge, split and secure — the upstream PDFCraft workbench running inside Astravia, on your own machine, with the document you opened in the workspace.

showcase.user_prompt: Open PDFCraft and turn the background of @assets/cover.png into a blue gradient.
showcase.assistant_reply: Cover loaded. Turning the background into a blue gradient now.

items.title: The real workbench
items.description: The panel serves the official PDFCraft web build byte for byte. Upstream's wasm and JavaScript are not patched; only two thin files of ours are added around them.

items.title: Open and save inside your project
items.description: Opening uses the file selected in the Explorer, and results are written back through Astravia instead of a downloads folder.

items.title: Nothing leaves the machine
items.description: The document is parsed locally in the tab. There is no account, no upload and no telemetry — the only network traffic is the one-time editor download.

items.title: Driven from the conversation
items.description: Ask in chat and the panel carries it out: pointer and keyboard steps run inside the editor one after another, each one named on the canvas while it happens.

items.title: Install the plugin
items.description: About 17 MB of editor files arrive on first open and are reused offline after that.

items.title: Open the PDFCraft tab
items.description: The preparation screen is the hub fetching its payload; later opens start from cache.

items.title: Select a PDF, then open it
items.description: File → Open inside the editor takes the file selected in Astravia rather than a system dialog.

items.title: Save the result back
items.description: The output goes through Astravia, so it can replace the source or become a new file.

blocks.content: Encryption and page operations happen in the browser sandbox, on your machine. A password you type is handled by upstream's code, never sent to the plugin's hub.
Interface language: the editor itself is English only — upstream ships no other language. The tab shell, the preparation page and this page follow your Astravia language.

Automation is an ordinary operation, not a macro player: a batch is a list of pointer and key steps the editor receives exactly as if they came from a hand, paced by frames so a press lasts a press. The canvas reports a text map and its average colour back, which is how the agent checks that a change really happened before reporting it.
